title: Can I BEAT the OLDEST Chess Website?
summary: Tony plays 3-minute blitz on FICS (Free Internet Chess Server, freechess.org), the oldest chess site still in original form (1995, pages unchanged since 2007), against real human players. The interface is retro: lightning/blitz/standard pools, timestamped announcements console, antique board and old-style piece art, per-move times on the left, no fancy bars. Goal: win one game; he wins all four, the last on time, and passes 2000 rating.
rules: Opponents are humans paired via a 'seek' (first: 'family' rated 1790).

board.theme_notes: Retro 1990s/2000s web UI: plain antique-looking board and old-style (classic Windows-era) pieces, text console with timestamped seek/announcement messages on the right, move-time list on the left; thumbnail is a plain white page with a blue underlined 'Play a Game' hyperlink and a hand cursor
